subject: Re: Synapse pilot — invoicing cadence, tax responsibility & OF redlines
messages:
From: Synapse Procurement <procurement@synapsehealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>; Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@synapsehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot order form — clarifications on invoicing & tax allocation

Hi Laura / Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are ready to move the 3-month pilot forward but have a few outstanding items on the Order Form and MSA redlines before procurement can approve:

- Invoicing cadence: Synapse prefers monthly invoices tied to usage, but your Order Form has an upfront quarterly invoice for the pilot. Can Redwood accept monthly invoicing for pilots?
- Net terms: we typically require net45 for pilots — is net30 the firm position or negotiable?
- Minimum commit: the Order Form references a 6-month minimum commit; for a 3-month pilot that is problematic. We propose a trial carveout or a one-time refundable credit if we terminate after the pilot.
- Taxes: Please confirm which party is responsible for VAT/withholding. We are US-based but have EU entities that could be billed.

Attached: Synapse_PO_Draft.pdf to start a PO conversation. Also looping Alex (CFO) and Jordan (GC will be on the next message).

Can you send a redline of the Order Form and a proposed invoice schedule by EOD Friday? Procurement needs this to align with our finance calendar.

Best,
Procurement Team
Synapse Health
[Attachment: Synapse_PO_Draft.pdf (PDF)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Synapse Procurement <procurement@synapsehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2027 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot order form — clarifications on invoicing & tax allocation

Hi — thanks for the clear ask and for sending the PO draft.

Quick answers up front:
- Monthly invoicing for the pilot: yes, we can do monthly invoicing for a pilot if we map the charges to a monthly usage cap. I attached a proposed Invoice_Schedule_Proposal.xlsx with a month-by-month billing cadence.
- Net terms: standard is net30, but we can consider net45 for this pilot on a one-off basis pending AP approval. Finance will confirm.
- Minimum commit: agree that 6-months shouldn’t apply to a 3-month pilot. We’ll propose a pilot carveout in the Order Form redline (refund or credit if terminated).
- Taxes: Redwood generally invoices gross; tax responsibility varies by entity. We will include a clause requiring Synapse to provide tax residency/evidence and we can treat withholding on a case-by-case basis.

I’ve asked Kimberly (contracts) and Aditya (sales leadership) to review the redline and confirm the commercial fallback positions.

Next steps:
1) Kimberly to share preferred redline language for pilot carveout and tax clause.
2) Redwood to send redlined Order Form + DocuSign link for signatures (if PO/terms align).
3) Synapse to confirm whether net45 is a hard requirement — please confirm by Friday so finance can triage.

Attached: Redline_OrderForm_Synapse_v1.docx, Invoice_Schedule_Proposal.xlsx

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Revenue Finance
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redline_OrderForm_Synapse_v1.docx (DOCX)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>; Synapse Procurement <procurement@synapsehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Dec 2027 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot order form — clarifications on invoicing & tax allocation

Hi all — I reviewed Laura's draft. High-level position below (will add inline redlines in the doc):

1) Pilot carveout / minimum commit
- Proposed language: "For the avoidance of doubt, the Order Form's Minimum Commitment shall not apply to the initial 3-month pilot term. If Customer elects to terminate at the end of the pilot, any prepaid amounts will be refunded pro rata or applied as a credit toward future usage, at Redwood's election."
- Alternative (if Finance needs guarantees): refundable security credit equal to one month's forecasted usage held for the term.

2) Invoicing cadence
- Accept monthly invoicing for the pilot provided usage is reported and billed in arrears (e.g., December usage invoiced Jan 1). If Synapse requires invoicing in advance, Redwood needs prepayment and an escrow holdback clause.

3) Net terms
- We can agree to net45 for this pilot only if Synapse provides a PO and standard commercial references. Default remains net30 for all future orders.

4) Taxes & Withholding
- Insert: Customer is responsible for taxes based on Customer's jurisdiction; Redwood will provide tax residency forms (W-9 or equivalent) on request. For EU billings, Redwood will invoice the entity specified by Customer and will not assume responsibility for reverse-charge or local withholding unless mutually agreed in writing.

5) Docs/Execution
- Once redlines are accepted, we'll send the final OF via DocuSign. If Synapse needs a signed MSA amendment, include a signature page in the envelope.

Laura — I left inline comments on liability wording and the credit/refund mechanics. Synapse — if you want the refundable-security option, let us know how you'd prefer the instrument (credit card hold vs escrow).

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Contracts Manager
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redline_OrderForm_Synapse_v1.docx (updated with comments)]

Quick commercial note from the sales side:
- Pricing: we'll honor the pilot discounted rate in the redline but need to preserve the right to revert to standard list for production. I'll add a short clause in the OF to make the pilot price non-precedential.
- Minimum commit workaround: recommending we do a "monthly cap" approach — set a monthly committed cap for the pilot and bill overage. That avoids full MSA minimums and keeps ops simple.

Synapse — Kimberly & Laura have covered the finance/legal asks. If you can confirm whether net45 is non-negotiable, I can scope the commercial concession (1–2% fee or extended payment schedule).

Thanks,

Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Meyers <jmeyers@synapsehealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>; Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>; Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@synapsehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 4 Dec 2027 11:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot order form — clarifications on invoicing & tax allocation

Kimberly / Laura — thanks for the fast turnaround. A few notes from Synapse legal / finance after reviewing your redline: 

- Net terms: net45 is Synapse policy for vendor pilots under $50k and is a standard AP requirement. We can do net30 for larger, multi-year agreements, but pilots are net45 unless otherwise approved by our treasury lead.
- PO: Attached is Synapse_PO_Draft.pdf with billing contact and remit address. We will need the final Order Form and invoice schedule to match the PO line items for our AP system.
- Tax evidence: we will share the EU entity information if invoicing crosses jurisdictions. We need Redwood to confirm whether Redwood will list VAT as a separate line item or include it in the invoice total. If VAT is applicable, Synapse may apply reverse-charge; we need Redwood's position on reverse-charge applicability.
- Minimum commit: we accept the pilot carveout language you proposed but ask that the refundable-credit option be the default — refundable to the billing entity within 30 days of termination.

Please return a redlined OF that: (a) shows the pilot carveout language, (b) switches to monthly arrears billing, and (c) indicates net45 as the invoice term for this pilot. If you cannot accept net45, please indicate the AP contact who will approve net45 on Redwood's side so we can expedite internal approval.

Jordan Meyers
General Counsel
Synapse Health
[Attachment: Synapse_PO_Draft_v2.pdf (PDF)]
